page: Amazon Web Services c7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware includes 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. It exhibits exceptional memory bandwidth, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only operations ranking in the top 10%. Cryptographic capabilities are highly performant, as evidenced by top-tier Passmark CPU encryption and extended instructions test results. For specialized workloads, it achieves top-tier performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput.

In language model inference, the c7a.metal-48xl achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds range from average to strong. Database operations, such as Redis SET, reach top-tier throughput. Given its compute-heavy 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and lack of local NVMe storage, this server is highly cost-efficient for raw parallel processing but less suited for memory-bound databases or workloads requiring local high-speed disk I/O. It is ideal for high-performance computing, software compilation, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
